input.summary: `getStackedOnPoints()` in the line series bails out with an empty array whenever the value dimension's *name* is falsy, so a dataset dimension literally named `''` produces an area polygon with zero baseline points (and `[NaN, NaN]` when `step` is used) instead of a rendered area. The guard must distinguish "there is no value dimension" (`undefined`/`null`) from "the value dimension is named with an empty string", i.e. change the truthiness check to a null check.
steps: WHY this is the right guard (verified by running the real chart under jest): `/workspace/src/chart/line/helper.ts:51` does `const valueDim = data.mapDimension(valueAxisDim);` and `SeriesData.mapDimension` (`/workspace/src/data/SeriesData.ts:500-509`) returns the dimension *name*. Measured values: for `dataset: {dimensions: ['cat', ''], ...}` it returns `''` (falsy but a valid dimension); for `series.encode: {y: -1}` it returns `undefined`. So `== null` still preserves the original protective intent while letting `''` through.

WHY the empty name is harmless downstream: `getStackedOnPoint` in `/workspace/src/chart/line/helper.ts:114-134` never reads `dataCoordInfo.valueDim` — it only uses `stacked`, `stackedOverDimension`, `valueStart`, `baseDataOffset` and `baseDim`. So once the early return is removed, the loop at LineView.ts:139-147 computes correct baseline points. Verified experimentally: with the current code the polygon gets `shape.points.length === 6` but `shape.stackedOnPoints.length === 0`; with the proposed guard the same option yields `[110, 220, 210, 220, 310, 220]` (baseline pinned to the axis zero line), which is exactly what an equivalent chart with a non-empty dimension name produces.

CONTEXT for the reviewer — the failure mode. `/workspace/src/chart/line/LineView.ts:673` does `let stackedOnPoints = isAreaChart && getStackedOnPoints(coordSys, data, dataCoordInfo);`.
